name: Victoria sponge
origin: Named for Queen Victoria, who was said to enjoy a slice with her afternoon tea; the standard British 'equal weights' formula, traditionally weighed as however many eggs are used, then matching weights of flour, sugar and butter.

ingredients.note: real recipes use self-raising flour; modelled here as its built-in raising agent, separated out into its own leavening-role line

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat softened butter and sugar until pale and fluffy

process.name: add eggs
process.description: beat in eggs one at a time

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in the self-raising flour (modelled as flour plus separate leavening) and salt

process.name: bake
process.description: divide between two sandwich tins and bake

notes: The 'four-four-four-four' equal-weights formula documented across standard British home-baking references (e.g. Mary Berry, Baking Bible; BBC Good Food's standard Victoria sponge ratio). The jam-and-cream filling that traditionally sandwiches the two layers is a separately-prepared component applied after baking (see catalog.ts's scope note) and is not part of this batter's formulation.
